Goal: turn the challenge into an engaging space mission game, combining imagination, strategy and technology.

Welcomes curious, motivated people who enjoy teamwork and thinking outside the box. All skills welcome! Let's build something amazing together!
summary:
Space Mission Design Studio is an interactive web-based simulation game that lets players step into the shoes of a NASA systems engineer to plan, launch, and manage robotic deep-space missions.

Directly addressing the "Space Mission Design Game" challenge, the app models real-world aerospace trade-offs across four scenarios—including the Lunar South Pole, Mars, and Europa. Players must balance mass, electrical power (accounting for solar inverse-square drop-off in the outer solar system), budget, and Deep Space Network data downlink constraints while selecting launch vehicles, power systems, antennas, and scientific instruments. Once launched, an animated orbital transfer tracks mission progress and tests players with mid-mission engineering anomalies.

By turning complex orbital mechanics and spacecraft subsystem constraints into hands-on gameplay, this tool makes NASA mission architecture accessible, engaging, and educational for students and space enthusiasts alike.
details:
What It Does & How It Works

Space Mission Design Studio is a browser-based interactive simulation game where players design, launch, and manage robotic deep-space missions. Players start by choosing one of four scenarios—Lunar South Pole Ice Scout, Mars Sample Return Relay Orbiter, Europa Subsurface Plume Explorer, or a Deep Space Sandbox.

In the spacecraft assembly phase, players pick a launch vehicle, an electrical power system, a Deep Space Network (DSN) antenna, and a suite of scientific instruments. As components are added or swapped, live telemetry gauges track four interdependent constraints: mass capacity, electrical wattage, financial budget, and daily data downlink throughput (GB/day). Once configured, players launch their spacecraft into an animated orbital transfer simulation featuring live flight logs, phase milestones, and mid-mission engineering anomalies that require real-time decision-making, followed by a post-mission performance debrief.

Benefits & Intended Impact

Space mission architecture is often taught through dense spreadsheets or simplified arcade games that ignore physics. This project bridges that gap by turning real aerospace systems engineering trade-offs into intuitive, hands-on gameplay. Its goal is to help students, educators, and space enthusiasts understand why NASA engineers make difficult compromises—such as sacrificing high-resolution cameras to stay within power limits or upgrading antennas to prevent science data bottlenecks—while connecting gameplay directly to real missions like LRO, MRO, and Europa Clipper.

Tools, Languages & Development Approach

  • Tech Stack: Built as a zero-dependency, single-file web application using HTML5, CSS3, Vanilla JavaScript, and the HTML5 Canvas API for real-time orbital trajectory rendering.

Creativity & Engineering Factors Considered

  • Real Orbital Physics ($1/r^2$ Solar Drop-Off): Solar array output dynamically scales with distance from the Sun, forcing players heading to Europa (~5.2 AU) to abandon solar panels in favor of Radioisotope Thermoelectric Generators (RTGs).
  • Subsystem Interdependencies & Synergies: Instruments don't just add points—they generate raw data that clogs the spacecraft's memory unless paired with a capable high-gain antenna, and complementary instruments unlock science synergy bonuses.
  • Dynamic Anomaly Management: Mid-flight failures (such as radiation-induced memory glitches or thermal spikes) test whether the player built enough engineering margin into their design to survive unexpected crises.
